answer: Sybil resistance is priced at enrollment, not argued. Each joining agent posts a bond keyed to a hardware beacon nonce, so a thousand sock puppets need a thousand distinct physical tokens, and half that bond burns on exit, pushing the campaign above expected profit. Reputation rides a thread across epochs: weight accrues only while a streak survives slashing. Honest agents verify the bond once, yet the marginal cost of one extra vote stays high along the adoption ridge, where cheap identity would otherwise compound into control.
